---
title: "Selective posterior analysis with parqpost"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Selective posterior analysis with parqpost}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(parqpost)
```

Save post-warmup posterior draws once in wide format. Each parameter element
has its own column, and draw identifiers are explicit.

```{r storage}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
samples <- posterior::as_draws_df(posterior::example_draws())
write_draws(samples, path)
draws <- open_draws(path)
draws
variables(draws)
```

The object above holds a lazy Arrow query. Selecting parameter families and
filtering identifiers changes that query without collecting draw values.

```{r selection}
selected <- draws |>
  select_draws(c("mu", "theta")) |>
  subset_draws(chain = 1:4, iteration = 51:100)

wide <- collect_draws(selected)
head(wide)
```

The collection step reads only selected columns and returns a posterior
`draws_df` with original identifiers. To put array indices into columns, use
spread expressions. Scalars are broadcast across array indices.

```{r spreading}
tidy <- spread_draws(selected, mu, theta[school])
head(tidy)
```

Use dplyr after spreading to compute derived quantities. Here the result remains
grouped by school.

```{r manipulation}
centered <- dplyr::mutate(tidy, centered = theta - mu)
head(centered)
```

Diagnostics need complete, equally indexed chains. The package orders draws
before delegating numerical calculations to posterior.

```{r diagnostics}
diagnose_draws(selected, variables = "theta")
```

For plots, compute exact equal-tailed intervals directly from the selected wide
columns. This avoids creating a long data frame with every draw and index.

```{r intervals}
intervals <- summarise_intervals(
  selected, theta[school], .width = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95)
)
intervals
```

Map `school` to the plot's position, `.value` to its point, `.lower` and `.upper`
to interval endpoints, and `.width` to interval width or opacity. For summaries
of derived quantities, use the in-memory data with tidybayes or dplyr.

Opening and selection are lazy; collecting, spreading, diagnostics, and interval
summaries materialize the required draws. Selected draws and expanded spread
results must fit in memory. Regex expressions, omitted dimensions, and `|`
widening are outside the supported spread syntax.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(path)
```
